title: Myntra Tech Threads 2026: Where AI, Velocity and Indian Fashion Collide
excerpt: At its Bengaluru conclave, Myntra pitched conversational discovery, creator-led shopping and an AI brand stack — arguing Indian fashion is now built in real time, not handed down from runways.
body:
• Myntra held its annual flagship brand conclave Tech Threads 2026 in Bengaluru on August 21, under the theme "Where Velocity Meets Voice" — positioning AI, creator-led commerce and rapid fulfilment as the forces reshaping Indian fashion.
  • The tech showcase included conversational discovery through Maya, inspiration-led shopping through Glamstream, AI styling assistance, precision sizing, and an AI-Powered Brand Stack that Myntra says compresses multi-week design lifecycles into minutes.
  • A marquee panel, "Building Brands for Velocity & Voice," brought together Mango, H&M India, Honasa Consumer, Arvind Fashions and Agilitas Sports leadership to discuss building brands on real-time consumer signals.
  • The evening runway, "The Pulse of Now," was built on live data of how India dresses — with Malaika Arora walking as showstopper for her co-created label Maejoy, and a Sania Mirza–Sunil Chhetri conversation rounding out the celebrity lineup.

India's fashion conversation no longer starts on international runways — it starts in shopping carts, comment sections and street style. That was the thesis on display at Myntra's Tech Threads 2026, the Flipkart-owned fashion platform's annual brand conclave in Bengaluru on August 21, where technology and culture shared equal billing under the theme "Where Velocity Meets Voice."

The tech pitch

Myntra used the conclave to showcase a stack of AI-led shopping tools: conversational product discovery through Maya, inspiration-led shopping through Glamstream, AI styling assistance, precision sizing and concept-based AI recommendations. For partner brands, the headline acts were the AI-Powered Brand Stack — which Myntra says can shrink design lifecycles from weeks to minutes — and a revamped partner app, Mitra, aimed at accelerating brand growth on the platform. M-Now, its rapid-fulfilment proposition, rounds out the pitch: inspiration, personalisation and speed as one loop.

"Myntra Tech Threads was a great opportunity to hear from our brand partners on how our tech-led innovations are propelling their journey on the platform to build for the evolving customer needs," said Sharon Pais, Head of Myntra. She pointed to Glamstream — "which blends shoppers, influencers, and culture for inspiration" — alongside AI-led personalisation and M-Now as the levers "helping brands build deeper salience with customer engagement and powering their growth at scale."

Brands at the table

The marquee panel, "Building Brands for Velocity & Voice," moderated by Pais, brought together Daniel López García (Chief Commercial Officer and board member, Mango), Varun Alagh (co-founder and CEO, Honasa Consumer), Helena Kuylenstierna (director, H&M India), Amisha Jain (MD and CEO, Arvind Fashions) and Abhishek Ganguly (co-founder and CEO, Agilitas Sports). The takeaway, per coverage of the event: sustainable brand growth now requires integrating real-time consumer signals, creator-led engagement and tech-led supply chains — with India viewed as strategically important globally rather than as an afterthought market.

The brand awards underscored a maturing domestic ecosystem: The Pant Project took Best D2C Brand, Comet was Disruptor Brand of the Year, Powerlook won Gen Z Brand of the Year, Zouk won Best Handbags, Mokobara took Best Travel Gear, Palmonas won Best Jewellery, Plum took Best Personal Care, Biba won Best Women's Ethnicwear and Jompers took Best Men's Ethnicwear. H&M was named Velocity Brand of the Year, Mango Best International Brand, Lakmé Best Beauty, Decathlon Best Sports Apparel and New Balance Best Sports Footwear.

"Fashion in India today isn't handed down, it's built in real time."

— ELLE India, on the Tech Threads thesis

The runway: data as the designer

The evening showcase, "The Pulse of Now," was staged as a runway built on real-time data of how India actually dresses, in four sequences: In My Cart (Y2K streetwear via Myntra FWD), Court in Bloom (tennis-inspired athleisure), Gen Win (Desi Grunge) and ETH'REAL (maximalist South Asian festive and bridal). Brands on the runway spanned Soch, Vastramay, Jompers, House of Pataudi, Taavi, Kalini, Mango, M&S, Snitch and Roadster. Malaika Arora closed the show as showstopper for Maejoy, her co-created label, while Sania Mirza and Sunil Chhetri appeared in a sport-and-leadership conversation moderated by Gaurav Kapur.

What's next

No launch dates were announced for Maya, Glamstream, the AI-Powered Brand Stack or the revamped Mitra — the conclave framed them as showcased innovations rather than dated rollouts. The test will be whether the "velocity and voice" thesis converts into shipped product: AI that genuinely shortens discovery, creators who genuinely move carts, and fulfilment fast enough to make the inspiration-to-purchase loop feel instant.

nri_angle: Ethnicwear was a strong awards and runway strand (Biba, House of Pataudi, Taavi) — contemporary Indian occasion wear the diaspora increasingly shops; the honoured homegrown D2C labels are ones diaspora readers seek out.
